svg.title: Evaluating Copilot answers with Fabric IQ
svg.desc: An engineer runs a local Python scorer with questions.yaml. In a live run the scorer signs in with a delegated Microsoft Entra test identity, calls Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat through Microsoft Graph beta, and receives the answer and citations. Any grounding in Fabric IQ reports and Power BI semantic models through the beta API depends on the tenant. The scorer separately runs reference DAX against the expected Sales Analytics model through Power BI executeQueries, never through Copilot. The other model, Sales Sandbox, is a decoy. Both models are backed by Contoso Lakehouse data. Workspace monitoring yields SemanticModelLogs DAX evidence matched by test user and time window; the match is heuristic, not causal proof. Replay feeds saved JSONL answers to the same value, citation and model checks; replay with --no-publish needs no tenant. The scorer always writes local JSONL and can also publish to an evaluation Eventhouse. Its EvalRuns, EvalResults and EvalQueries tables are made available in OneLake and exposed through Lakehouse table shortcuts and a SQL analytics endpoint. A Fabric App built with Rayfin queries that endpoint through the read-only fabric-sqlanalytics connector for its Overview and Questions pages.

Only where the tenant supports it

path.aria-label: Run reference DAX directly against only Sales Analytics using Power BI executeQueries, independently of Copilot
The expected model returns the reference value to the scorer
Power BI model query events are available to workspace monitoring
Contoso Lakehouse data backs the semantic models
Read SemanticModelLogs in the source-data workspace
DAX evidence is returned to the scorer; attribution by test user and time window is heuristic

The Fabric App reads the SQL endpoint through fabric-sqlanalytics, a read-only connector
